subcomponents.title: Skill instructions and templates

criteria.rationale: Every template the skill materializes would type-check and build at its documented destination. I established this two ways: tracing each template against the bootstrapped layout and the kit's types, and a focused materialize-and-build test. Destination: SKILL.md §3a and `newPresentation` in presentation-tool.mjs write the five templates to `src/presentations/<slug>/` (Talk.tsx, entities.ts, styles.css) and `src/presentations/<slug>/steps/` (index.ts, scene.tsx). The registry entry is `import('./<slug>/Talk.tsx')`. Relative imports: all resolve inside `src`. - From `src/presentations/<slug>/Talk.tsx`, `../../presentation-kit/Presentation.tsx` is `src/presentation-kit/Presentation.tsx`. `./steps/index.ts` and `./styles.css` are siblings. - From `steps/index.ts` and `steps/scene.tsx`, `../../../presentation-kit/...` is `src/presentation-kit/...`. `../entities.ts` is the presentation folder's own file. - From `entities.ts`, `../../presentation-kit/nodes/props.ts` exists and exports `Placement`. CSS import: `./styles.css` is produced from `styles.css.tmpl`. Vite types come from `types: ["vite/client"]` in tsconfig.app.json. Required props, checked against the kit: - `Presentation` (Presentation.tsx and `PresentationProps` in types.ts): `steps` and `title` are the only required props. The template passes both, plus optional `initialMode="browse"` and `className`. `Mode` is `'browse' | 'present'` in constants.ts, so `"browse"` is valid. - `Appear` (Appear.tsx): only `children`, which the scene template provides. - `Box`, `Label`, `SymbolChip`, `Frame` and `Emphasis`: their props extend `NodeProps`, whose only required field is `id`. The scene template passes `id`, `at`, `className`, `Icon`, `label` and children, all declared (`Icon?: LucideIcon` and `label?: string` on Box, `Icon?` on SymbolChip). - `Arrow`: requires `id`, `from` and `to`. The template passes all three, using `e.from!` and `e.to!`. - `SceneLayer`: only optional props. Field names: - The `Step` fields are `id`, `era`, `title`, `caption`, `Scene`, `payload` and `groupKey`, all in `Step` in types.ts. `Scene` is typed `Step<null>` and takes `SceneProps<null>`. - `Placement` fields are `x`, `y`, `w` and `h`. - `lucide-react` and `motion` are in the bootstrap package.json. Compiler flags: tsconfig.app.json sets `noUnusedLocals`, `noUnusedParameters`, `erasableSyntaxOnly` and `verbatimModuleSyntax`. The templates use `import type` for types, import only what they use, and have no enums or parameter properties. The `Rendered` switch covers every `EntityKind`. Placeholders: `fill` in presentation-tool.mjs replaces `__SLUG__`, `__TITLE_JSON__` and `__TITLE__`. `__TITLE_JSON__` expands to a JSON string literal inside a JSX expression. `__TITLE__` appears only in a CSS comment, with `*/` neutralised. Focused test: tests/integration/bootstrap.test.ts bootstraps into a temp directory outside the repo. It runs `TOOL new` with a hostile title (`'Say "hi" \\ */ {x} <b>'`), runs `npm ci`, `npm run build` (tsc -b plus vite build) and `npm run lint`, then `npm run verify`. It asserts both `starter: rendered 2 steps` and `quoted-title: rendered 2 steps`. That builds and renders the materialized presentation templates. The inspect template at `templates/bootstrap/scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs` is copied to `scripts/` with `scripts/lib/preview.mjs` alongside it. The same test asserts the bootstrap copies of these scripts are byte-aligned with the repo copies.

criteria.rationale: The record exercised many scenarios at the tool and app level: standalone and monorepo scaffolding, present/browse toggle, keyboard, swipe, jump, boundaries, 390 and 1280 viewports, and the registry edge. Agent-dialogue journeys are disclosed as environmental, so they do not count against coverage. A substantial block of user-visible behavior that the environment allowed was still left unexercised, and the log discloses it as a choice rather than an impediment. Unexercised items: morph, newcomer and exit motion ("not conclusively observed"); bare kit style hooks and unstyled output; coordinate-heavy raw-motion scenes; typed payload at the boundary; partial scaffold; controlled overlap-warning and allow-overlap fixtures; exact normative title/caption comparison; and the verification failure cases (missing sample, console or page error, step error). The verification failure cases were skipped citing the acceptance skill's ban on automated suites, but the log gives no reason a fixture could not be run. Rounds 1 and 2 were diff-scoped retests and add no new first-pass coverage. Taken together, the chosen omissions leave a substantial share of the specs' user-visible behavior unexercised.

criteria.rationale: Requirement: every material claim must be backed by verified candidate artifacts, in every candidate record including the assumptions ledger, and attributing a result to the implementation run does not prove it. The assumptions ledger (packet.txt:2919-2924) states that the kit's general morph, entry-delay and exit behavior "is proven by kit unit tests against fixtures". That claim maps to three basis scenarios: "Persisting entity morphs", "New entity enters after others settle" and "Departing entity exits". The packet has no artifact for it: no unit-test run, no output and no log. The exploration log says instead that the acceptance pass saw only settled states, that exit and newcomer timing were "not conclusively observed" (2640), and that no direct morph or timing observation was made (2673). It also says no `npm test` was run (2699, 2732). Judge C's reason therefore holds and decides the criterion. Judges A and B are right that the log's own observations state actions and results (P toggle, swipe, jumps, clamps, detect/bootstrap/new/build, round-2 measurements) and that the log discloses the motion gaps. But the criterion weighs the ledger's claim regardless of author. A disclosure in the log does not turn the ledger's affirmative "is proven" into a limitation. A and B's reasons do not address that claim, so they do not satisfy the requirement.

votes.rationale: The verifier reserves an ephemeral port and uses --strictPort, but it releases the port before spawning. The child is spawned with stdio 'ignore', so there is no announcement from the child. Readiness is plain HTTP polling of that port, and the only ownership check is `child.exitCode !== null`, sampled before each fetch. Another server that grabbed the released port could answer with 200 before the child's exit is observed. Neither accepted mechanism is present: readiness is not taken from the child's own announcement, and polling is not raced against the child's exit event. A strict port alone is insufficient.

votes.rationale: A missing or non-numeric data-step-count becomes NaN or 0, and `!(count >= 1)` throws a render failure, so an unreadable count cannot pass with no steps checked. The transition check compares the attribute string to String(i+1), and a null hook never equals it, so a missing or non-numeric hook is never counted as progress (no Number(null)===0 coercion). votes.rationale: Props are typed from the rendered element: NodeProps extends HTMLAttributes, ArrowProps extends SVGAttributes, SceneLayerProps extends HTMLAttributes. Every primitive spreads `...rest` first and then applies layoutId, data-presentation-id/node and data-presentation-state, so callers cannot override them. Kit-only props (Icon, label, state, at, from, to, bend, bidirectional) are destructured and not forwarded to the DOM.

SymbolChip.tsx: `data-presentation-state={state}` comes after {...rest}, and state is destructured
Arrow.tsx: `<svg {...rest} width=... data-presentation-node="arrow" data-presentation-id={id}>` with from/to/bend/bidirectional destructured

votes.rationale: All three clauses hold for every public primitive: Box, Frame, Label, Emphasis, SymbolChip, Arrow, SceneLayer and Appear. (1) Typed props: node primitives take NodeProps, which extends Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>, ...> in props.ts, with BoxProps and SymbolChipProps extending it. Arrow takes Omit<SVGAttributes<SVGSVGElement>, 'id'|'from'|'to'>, and SceneLayer takes HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>. Appear takes only { children: ReactNode } and has no passthrough props. None uses Record<string, unknown>. (2) Identity hooks after caller props: Box, Frame, Label, Emphasis and SymbolChip spread {...rest} first, then {...entityProps(kind, id, at, style)}. That supplies layoutId, transition, data-presentation-node and data-presentation-id, so caller values cannot override them. SymbolChip sets data-presentation-state after rest. Arrow spreads {...rest} before width, height, viewBox, data-presentation-node and data-presentation-id. SceneLayer spreads {...rest} before data-presentation-layer. votes.rationale: The verifier reserves an ephemeral port and uses --strictPort, but it releases the port before spawning. The child is spawned with stdio 'ignore', so there is no announcement from the child. Readiness is plain HTTP polling of that port, and the only ownership check is `child.exitCode !== null`, sampled before each fetch. Another server that grabbed the released port could answer with 200 before the child's exit is observed. Neither accepted mechanism is present: readiness is not taken from the child's own announcement, and polling is not raced against the child's exit event. A strict port alone is insufficient.

votes.rationale: Every template the skill materializes would type-check and build at its documented destination. I established this two ways: tracing each template against the bootstrapped layout and the kit's types, and a focused materialize-and-build test. Destination: SKILL.md §3a and `newPresentation` in presentation-tool.mjs write the five templates to `src/presentations/<slug>/` (Talk.tsx, entities.ts, styles.css) and `src/presentations/<slug>/steps/` (index.ts, scene.tsx). The registry entry is `import('./<slug>/Talk.tsx')`. Relative imports: all resolve inside `src`. - From `src/presentations/<slug>/Talk.tsx`, `../../presentation-kit/Presentation.tsx` is `src/presentation-kit/Presentation.tsx`. `./steps/index.ts` and `./styles.css` are siblings. - From `steps/index.ts` and `steps/scene.tsx`, `../../../presentation-kit/...` is `src/presentation-kit/...`. `../entities.ts` is the presentation folder's own file. - From `entities.ts`, `../../presentation-kit/nodes/props.ts` exists and exports `Placement`. CSS import: `./styles.css` is produced from `styles.css.tmpl`. Vite types come from `types: ["vite/client"]` in tsconfig.app.json. Required props, checked against the kit: - `Presentation` (Presentation.tsx and `PresentationProps` in types.ts): `steps` and `title` are the only required props. The template passes both, plus optional `initialMode="browse"` and `className`. `Mode` is `'browse' | 'present'` in constants.ts, so `"browse"` is valid. - `Appear` (Appear.tsx): only `children`, which the scene template provides. - `Box`, `Label`, `SymbolChip`, `Frame` and `Emphasis`: their props extend `NodeProps`, whose only required field is `id`. The scene template passes `id`, `at`, `className`, `Icon`, `label` and children, all declared (`Icon?: LucideIcon` and `label?: string` on Box, `Icon?` on SymbolChip). - `Arrow`: requires `id`, `from` and `to`. The template passes all three, using `e.from!` and `e.to!`. - `SceneLayer`: only optional props. Field names: - The `Step` fields are `id`, `era`, `title`, `caption`, `Scene`, `payload` and `groupKey`, all in `Step` in types.ts. `Scene` is typed `Step<null>` and takes `SceneProps<null>`. - `Placement` fields are `x`, `y`, `w` and `h`. - `lucide-react` and `motion` are in the bootstrap package.json. lines.text: ## Sample entities: "never rearranged" vs "morph in place"
- **Question:** The sample spec says entities accumulate and are never rearranged, but AT-003 asks to observe persisting entities morph and departing entities exit.
- **Requirement:** "Committed reference sample" intro; "Stable entities morph across steps"; AT-003.

- **Ruling:** In the sample, persisting entities keep their canvas coordinates across steps; only state changes (labels, emphasis flags, the green check, the flagged edited card) morph. All nine steps share one scene group. Departing-entity behavior in the sample is observed when navigating backward. The kit's general morph, entry-delay and exit behavior is proven by kit unit tests against fixtures.
- **Rationale:** Honours the normative sample description without weakening the kit contract.

- **Step narration and identity; ordered sample and numbering:** The production preview exposed nine ordered steps with titles/captions; AXI snapshot showed `01 / 09` and the active title/caption. Inspector reached and captured all nine indices. Exact comparison of every rendered title/caption against the normative strings was **not performed**.

- **Typed payload boundary:** **Not independently exercised.** A passing TypeScript production build is evidence that the committed sample typechecks, not that a new grouped custom payload needs no cast in an independent consumer.

- **Persistent entities, newcomer/departure animation, grouped persistence and intentional composition:** Wide settled screenshots show accumulation and preserved placements across first, dense and final states. No recording or bounding-box comparison was made during the actual transition; exit and newcomer timing were **not conclusively observed**. The artifact and state model are documented in `round-0-wide/` captures.

- Full user interview, partial-detail opt-in, ASCII mockup behavior, confirmation dialogue, ambiguous modification selection and scoped agent edit: no live user or separate agent runner; tool-level results cannot establish agent compliance.
- Agent repair/recheck workflow for seeded build/render/visual faults: not performed, so the agent was not credited for self-repair.

- `npm run verify`, automated integration/E2E suites, fault-injected verifier cases, and process-cleanup assertions: excluded by the acceptance skill's instruction not to run automated suites. The isolated production app was built and browsed manually via AXI and the local screenshot helper.

- Controlled overlap-warning and allow-overlap fixtures; exact text style/no-default checks in a bare kit-only app; direct morph bounding-box/timing observation; exact normative string-by-string sample comparison; custom typed-payload consumer compile: no focused controlled fixture was created for these.

- No full AT-001/AT-002/AT-004 agent workflow was repeated; this round is diff-sized, and the interactive skill journeys were not touched by the diff. Round-0 history already records the agent-interaction evidence limitation.

- No `npm test`, lint, `npm run verify`, integration suite, Validator or CI poll was run. The acceptance skill excludes automated suites, and the open narrow-readability finding means CI polling is not entered until no finding remains.
- No additional parser cases beyond the prior trailing-array failure and the empty typed-array case; no registry form generated dynamically rather than declared as an array literal.
- No full transition recording or per-entity coordinate comparison. The diff changed sample typography and entity box dimensions only; screenshots show settled composition.

candidate_reported_ci.verbatim: ## Slow tests: the test plan says "every pull request", CLAUDE.md says no CI
- **Question:** Where do INT-001, INT-002, E2E-001 and E2E-002 run, given test-plan.md says "on every pull request" and CLAUDE.md forbids CI configuration and keeps `npm test` fast?

- **Ruling:** The suites are npm scripts and no workflow file is added. `npm test` runs only the Vitest unit and contract tests. A separate script (`test:integration`) runs INT-001, INT-002 and E2E-002. `npm run verify` is E2E-001. "Every pull request" means "part of the documented pre-completion gate", not hosted CI.
- **Question:** What does "identifying which check failed" look like, and how long may a transition take?

- **Ruling:** Every file under `src/presentation-kit/` is byte-identical to its copy in `skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/`, with a contract test that fails on any difference. The template carries its own `package-lock.json` so `npm ci` works.

No CI was polled because two clear acceptance findings remain. The repository instructions specify no hosted workflow configuration; current-head CI is therefore recorded as **not checked / no hosted CI configuration supplied**, not as a pass. Tracked source remained unchanged during acceptance. See `acceptance-handoff.md` for the decision and limitations.

- No `npm test`, lint, `npm run verify`, integration suite, Validator or CI poll was run. The acceptance skill excludes automated suites, and the open narrow-readability finding means CI polling is not entered until no finding remains.
CI was not polled because finding 1 remains open. Repository instructions state that no hosted CI configuration is part of this project. No current-head CI pass is claimed.

3. **Bootstrap parity/materialization.** Prediction: all non-test canonical kit files remain byte-aligned with the bootstrap copy, and a standalone copy builds with the changed narrow-gutter implementation. All 24 non-test kit files matched byte-for-byte. `npm ci` and `npm run build` passed in the copied bootstrap. The two registry edge variants above also built after generation. No finding.

Current local HEAD and PR head both equal `248ea01499e5065933a829c995767cba94a4725a`; local branch tracks origin and tracked worktree is clean. `gh pr checks` reports `CodeRabbit pass`, with detail “Review skipped: draft pull request”; `gh pr view` reports the same head SHA but `mergeable=CONFLICTING`, `mergeStateStatus=DIRTY`. The PR comments helper reports no actionable comments and no unresolved threads; it reports only CodeRabbit's informational draft-skip message. Repository guidance says no hosted CI configuration is present, so current-head automated CI coverage is absent. The bundled `wait-ci` status script was also incompatible with the installed GitHub CLI (`baseRefOid` is not an accepted `gh pr view --json` field; `gh pr checks --json` is not supported). Supported `gh pr checks`/`gh pr view` queries supplied current-head status evidence, but the PR merge conflict is an unresolved acceptance impediment. No conflict paths were available from those queries.

No hosted CI workflows are configured for this repository, consistent with repository guidance; current-head automated CI coverage is absent. `gh pr checks` reports one CodeRabbit status as pass, but its detail says “Review skipped: draft pull request”, so it is not validation evidence. The PR comments helper found no actionable comments or unresolved threads. The bundled `wait-ci` checker was incompatible with the installed GitHub CLI's supported JSON fields/options; supported `gh pr view` and `gh pr checks` queries still established the current head, status and merge conflict. No automated-validation evidence was supplied for this pass.
- **Expected:** The PR head matching local HEAD should be mergeable before acceptance CI handoff.
